ev.a_good_harvest.text.1: The barley stood like a wall, the ears heavy and rustling. For the first time in years the granary can't hold the harvest, and you sleep soundly.
ev.a_good_harvest.text.2: A generous year: the olive trees bend under their fruit, and the press creaks until late at night. The whole house smells of fresh oil.
ev.a_good_harvest.text.1.egypt: The Nile rose exactly as much as it should — it neither drowned the village nor left the fields dry. The wheat came up so thick that even the tax collector smiled for a moment.
ev.a_good_harvest.text.2.egypt: This year the date palms bowed under their fruit, and the flax in your fields grew waist-high. There will be enough for the tax and for a feast.
ev.a_money_quarrel.text: {npc} counted the coins in the jar and asked where half of them had gone. You had to confess to the new sandals — and then hear about the sandals until midnight.
ev.a_first_word.text: {npc} said {g=npc_sex:his|her} first word. It wasn't "mama" or "papa" but the name of the neighbors' dog — and you still told the whole street about it.
ev.a_friend_wedding.text: {npc} is getting married. You danced at the door until you were hoarse, and the next morning you couldn't remember half the songs — probably the better half.
ev.a_friend_wedding.text.rome: {npc} is getting married. The bride was led by torchlight to the groom's house, boys scrambled for the nuts thrown by custom, and you shouted "Talassio!" with everyone else without ever learning what it means.
ev.a_friend_wedding.text.athens: {npc} is getting married. The bride rode in a cart by torchlight, and you walked behind singing the wedding hymn until your voice gave out.
ev.a_bad_cough.text.1: A cough tormented you all winter. The neighbor recommended honey with garlic, the doctor honey with vinegar. It was probably the honey that helped.
ev.a_bad_cough.text.2: You spent a week in bed with aches and fever. The household didn't collapse without you — which was almost insulting.
ev.a_lucky_sale.text: A wealthy traveler bought everything on your stall, even the things laid out just for show. He seemed to have no idea how to haggle — and you didn't teach him.
ev.a_stolen_tunic.text: While you were warming up at the baths, someone walked off with your best tunic. You had to go home in a stranger's threadbare cloak, wishing the thief every misfortune you could name.
ev.a_stolen_tunic.text.rome: While you were warming up at the baths, someone walked off with your best tunic. Next morning you paid to have a curse scratched onto a lead tablet: may the thief not sleep until it's returned.
ev.a_dinner_guests.text: The guests dropped by "for an hour." They left after midnight, having eaten everything down to the spare flatbreads and praising your table loudly enough for the whole street to hear.
ev.a_eclipse.text: In broad daylight the sun went dark, as if someone had cupped a hand over it. Dogs howled, priests cried out, then the light came back — and everyone pretended they hadn't been frightened at all.
ev.a_rain_roof.text: A downpour broke in the night, and the roof remembered every one of its cracks. Until morning you kept setting out pots, and the drops drummed on them in different voices.
ev.a_letter_relative.text: {npc} sent a letter from a distant city: alive, well, asking for a warm cloak and telling you not to believe the rumors. Which rumors, the letter doesn't say.
ev.a_letter_relative.text.egypt: {npc} sent a letter on papyrus. It opens as it should — "Before all else, I pray that you are in good health" — and ends with a request for cheese and a pair of sandals.
ev.a_sailor_dolphins.text: For half a day a pod of dolphins raced along the bow, leaping out of the water. The old helmsman said it meant fair weather — and for the first time you can remember, he was right.
ev.a_scribe_blot.text: You knocked the inkpot over an almost finished scroll. Three days of work spread into a blot shaped like a sea monster. You were copying it again until dawn.
ev.a_grateful_patient.text: The stonecutter whose shoulder you set came to thank you: a live goose under his arm and stories of your skill for everyone he meets. The goose still hisses at you.
ev.a_long_march.text: Twenty miles a day with palisade stakes, a cooking pot and days of grain on your back — and in the evening, the camp ditch still to dig. Your legs throb, but you fall asleep the moment you lie down.
ev.a_midwife_night.text: The labor lasted all night; by morning even the mother's grandmother had stopped giving advice. You didn't give up — and at dawn a healthy boy was crying, and his mother fell asleep, alive and exhausted.
ev.a_merchant_route.text: A mule driver showed you a mountain path your competitors haven't heard of yet. It's four days shorter — and a whole cartload of fodder cheaper.
ev.a_dye_vat.text: You finally got an even, deep blue — the neighbor women come to look at the wool as if it were a miracle. Your arms, though, will stay blue to the elbow for another week.
ev.a_crowd_chant.text: Today the stands chanted your name. Next morning someone had scratched it on a tavern wall beside a palm branch, the victor's sign. In this city, fame is written with charcoal and a nail.
ev.a_garrison_dice.text: Garrison life is dull: guard duty, porridge, dice. You won the squad leader's best cloak — and by nightfall lost it back, along with your own.
ev.a_garrison_dice.text.egypt: A garrison on the edge of the desert: guard duty, heat and dice in the evenings. You won the squad leader's best cloak — and by nightfall lost it back, along with your own.
ev.a_goat_vineyard.text: Your goat squeezed into the neighbor's vineyard and ate everything it could reach. The neighbor wants compensation, the goat is satisfied, and you are not.
ev.a_harbor_wages.text: Three ships came into harbor at once, and there weren't enough hands. You hauled cargo until dark, and the foreman paid double without haggling.
ev.a_big_order.text: The temple ordered three hundred clay lamps from you for the festival. For a month you worked without straightening your back, and now you see lamps even in your dreams.
ev.a_kitchen_figs.text: The old cook slipped you a handful of dried figs and winked. A small thing — but in this house even small things don't belong to you, and so you remember it for a long time.
ev.a_harvest_song.text: At the harvest someone began a song in the language of a faraway homeland, and a dozen voices joined in. The overseer didn't understand a word, and for the first time in ages you smiled.
ev.a_temple_omen.text: You checked three times that the altar fire burned evenly and the knife was clean. The omens came out favorable, and the crowd at the temple let out its breath together with you.
ev.a_temple_omen.text.egypt: Cats sacred to the goddess Bastet live in the temple courtyard, and one of them has chosen your lap. You are now the most revered person in the temple: a holy animal sleeps on you.
ev.a_rhetor_applause.text: Your speech in court drew such laughter and applause that the court had to call for silence. Your client won, though he never quite understood what you said.
ev.a_steward_accounts.text: The estate steward swears that mice ate forty sacks of grain. Judging by the evidence, they were large mice, with a cart and good friends at the market.
ev.a_wool_basket.text: You sat down at the spindle among the maids yourself — let them see the mistress can do more than count other people's work. By evening your fingers ache, but today the wool was spun twice as fast.
ev.a_wool_basket.text.rome: You sat down at the spindle among the maids yourself. A worthy Roman woman's tombstone says it briefly: "She kept the house, she worked the wool" — and you wouldn't mind earning those words one day.
ev.a_salutatio.text: From dawn, petitioners crowd your door. One wants a post for his nephew, another a delay on his taxes, a third simply wishes to be seen standing next to you.
ev.a_child_puppy.text: {npc} dragged home a stray puppy and swears it will guard the house. So far it is diligently guarding only your sandal — and has already chewed through half of it.
ev.a_mother_visit.text: {npc}, your mother, came with a basket of flatbreads and a year's worth of advice. The flatbreads were gone that evening; the advice will stay with you longer.
ev.a_father_story.text: {npc}, your father, is telling yet again how he nearly got rich as a young man. Every year the ship in the story gets bigger and the storm more terrible.
ev.a_sibling_baby.text: {npc} has become a {g=npc_sex:father|mother}, and you an {g:uncle|aunt}. The baby was named after its grandfather and screams just as loudly as he does.
ev.a_spouse_stars.text: On a stifling evening {npc} called you out to sit in the courtyard. You barely spoke, just watched the stars and listened to the crickets — and it was one of the best evenings of the year.
ev.a_friend_tavern.text: {npc} dragged you into a tavern for "just one cup." It came to five, and the argument over whose neighborhood is better was never settled — even though you live on the same street.
ev.a_neighbor_noise.text.1: The neighbor behind the wall is banging away at night again. At first you thought he was mending furniture; now you suspect he's building a ship.
ev.a_neighbor_noise.text.2: The neighbor's donkey brays at dawn loud enough to wake the whole street. Its owner insists the donkey is simply very pious and greets the sun.
ev.a_neighbor_noise.text.3: Behind the wall someone's birthday was celebrated until morning. You weren't invited, but you now know all the songs by heart.
ev.a_rival_seen.text: {npc} walked past you in the market in a new cloak and pretended not to see you. You pretended too — but, it seems, less convincingly.
ev.a_child_better.text: Today, for the first time, {npc} did the work better than you — and didn't even notice. All evening you grumbled, and all evening you were proud.
ev.a_pharos_light.text: At night you saw the fire of the Pharos lighthouse burning over Alexandria, higher than any temple. They say it can be seen from far out at sea, and tonight that is easy to believe.
ev.a_comedy.text: A comedy was on at the Theater of Dionysus. A masked actor mimicked a famous politician so well that the man himself laughed loudest in the front row — at least until the play was over.
ev.a_new_fountain.text: A fountain opened at your crossroads, fed by water that travels from far away along an aqueduct. No more hauling buckets across half the city, and the neighbor women trade news right by the spout.
ev.a_partner_cheat.title: Double Books
ev.a_partner_cheat.text: For two years your partner has been doctoring the shared accounts. Under a floorboard you found the second, real tablet of records — and you didn't like the sum on it at all.
ev.a_partner_cheat.quiet: Part ways quietly, leaving the share
ev.a_partner_cheat.cheat_back.success: You beat the swindler at their own game. The money came back — with interest.
ev.a_partner_cheat.cheat_back.failure: The trick came out, and now it's you the market calls a cheat.
ev.a_rival_revenge.title: An Old Grudge
ev.a_rival_revenge.text: {npc}, whom you once exposed, has not forgotten the shame. Now {g=npc_sex:he|she} whispers to every customer that your goods are rotten and your word worthless.
ev.a_rival_revenge.strike_back.success: In front of witnesses you reminded the town of the old story of the forged accounts. The gossip died down.
ev.a_rival_revenge.strike_back.failure: The gossip proved stronger than the truth. Customers are going elsewhere.
ev.a_rival_revenge.make_peace: Come to make peace with a jug of wine
ev.a_rival_old.title: Years Later
ev.a_rival_old.text: {npc}, your old enemy, has grown old and gone broke: the warehouse burned, the children moved away. They say {g=npc_sex:he|she} has been asking about you — without malice.
ev.a_rival_old.pass_by: Walk on: to each their own
ev.a_moneylender.title: The Moneylender
ev.a_moneylender.text: The money ran out before the winter did. The moneylender by the temple will give you as much as you ask — at interest that turns the neighbors' beards gray at the mere mention.
ev.a_moneylender.ask_kin: Ask your kin for a loan
ev.a_moneylender_returns.title: Debt with Interest
ev.a_moneylender_returns.text: The old moneylender is dead, but his son remembers every coin. He arrives with a tablet in hand: over the years your debt has nearly doubled.
ev.a_moneylender_returns.work_off: Work off the debt in his shop
ev.a_moneylender_returns.court.success: The judge found the interest excessive. You repaid only what you borrowed — plus a little for the trouble.
ev.a_moneylender_returns.court.failure: The court sided with the lender. You had to hand over nearly everything in the house.
ev.a_foundling.title: A Basket at the Gate
ev.a_foundling.text: At dawn someone left a baby in a basket at the temple gate. This is how the poor give up children they cannot feed: whoever picks the child up will raise it.
ev.a_foundling.find_family.success: The potter's wife, who had prayed to the gods for a child for years, wept with joy as she took the basket.
ev.a_foundling.find_family.failure: No one wanted another mouth to feed. You left the baby with the temple attendants and couldn't sleep for a long time.
ev.a_foundling_grown.title: The Foundling
ev.a_foundling_grown.text: The child you once picked up at the temple gate has grown up. The neighbors whisper behind your back, and the questions you have avoided for so long are about to be asked out loud.
ev.a_foundling_grown.truth.success: A long silence, then an embrace: "So you chose me yourself."
ev.a_foundling_grown.truth.failure: The truth was heavy. For months the house spoke in low voices.
ev.a_temptation.title: Temptation
ev.a_temptation.text: {g:The young widow of an oil merchant|A traveling spice merchant} laughs at your jokes longer than politeness requires and invites you to drop by in the evening "to look at the goods." And at home, {npc} is waiting.
ev.a_temptation.go.success: No one found out. Only now your heart beats out of step with your home.
ev.a_temptation.go.failure: The town is small and tongues are long. At home you were met with a silence worse than shouting.
ev.a_temptation.tell_spouse: Tell the whole story at home, laughing
ev.a_temptation.tell_spouse.success: You laughed half the evening. You even seem to be a little bit envied — and that's nice.
ev.a_temptation.tell_spouse.failure: It wasn't funny. Now every trip you make to the market is followed by a long look.
ev.a_affair_letter.title: Old Notes
ev.a_affair_letter.text: A former servant of that very house brings a bundle of your old notes on wax tablets and hints that they are worth money. Otherwise, the wrong people may read them.
ev.a_affair_letter.refuse.success: He grumbled and left. The tablets seem to have vanished somewhere in his junk.
ev.a_affair_letter.refuse.failure: The notes reached your home. There was no point in excuses.
ev.a_child_match.title: A Match
ev.a_child_match.text: {npc} is of an age to marry. Wealthy neighbors propose a match: {g=npc_sex:the bride is no longer young and has a sharp tongue, but the dowry is generous|the groom is twice her age, but his house wants for nothing}. And your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} has long had eyes for the poor potter's {g=npc_sex:daughter|son}.
ev.a_match_wealthy_later.title: Useful In-Laws
ev.a_match_wealthy_later.text: The in-laws you married into for advantage keep their word: their connections open the right doors for you. Only your child, when visiting, says less and less.
ev.a_match_heart_later.title: Cramped and Merry
ev.a_match_heart_later.text: Your child's home is cramped, poor and noisy — and every time you visit, you hear laughter. The love match has proved stronger than many profitable ones.
ev.a_lawsuit.title: A Lawsuit
ev.a_lawsuit.text: Your neighbor demands compensation: your donkey, he says, trampled his vegetable garden. He has two witnesses, both of them his cousins.
ev.a_lawsuit.text.rome: Your neighbor demands compensation: your donkey, he says, trampled his vegetable garden. He summoned you before the praetor right in the middle of the street, in front of everyone, and both his witnesses are his cousins.
ev.a_lawsuit.text.athens: Your neighbor has filed suit: your donkey, he says, trampled his vegetable garden. Hundreds of citizen jurors will decide, and they favor whoever speaks more beautifully.
ev.a_lawsuit.text.egypt: Your neighbor has petitioned the strategos: your donkey, he says, trampled his vegetable garden. The official demands that you answer, and both the neighbor's witnesses are his cousins.
ev.a_lawsuit.advocate: Hire someone who knows the law
ev.a_lawsuit.advocate.success: Your advocate tangled the witnesses up so skillfully that they began arguing with each other. Case dismissed.
ev.a_lawsuit.advocate.failure: The advocate took the money and lost. Now you have to pay both him and the neighbor.
ev.a_lawsuit.self.success: You asked how a donkey had climbed a fence as tall as a man. Even the judges laughed.
ev.a_lawsuit.self.failure: You stumbled over your words and lost your temper. The ruling went to the neighbor.
ev.a_inheritance.title: Father's Grove
ev.a_inheritance.text: The inheritance isn't divided yet, and {npc} already claims the whole olive grove: "I looked after the old man while you were off who knows where." And {g=npc_sex:he|she} is not entirely wrong.
ev.a_inheritance.court: Go to court for your share
ev.a_inheritance.court.success: The court awarded you more than half. You won the grove and lost your family.
ev.a_inheritance.court.failure: The case dragged on, the money went into it, and your family stopped greeting you.
ev.a_sibling_reconcile.title: A Cart at the Gate
ev.a_sibling_reconcile.text: {npc} never forgot how you once gave up Father's grove. In a lean year {g=npc_sex:he|she} came to you unasked, with a cart full of oil and grain.
ev.a_voyage.title: A Long Voyage
ev.a_voyage.text: A captain you know is taking passengers with goods on a long voyage. Those who come back will sell at three times the price. Those who don't won't care either way.
ev.a_voyage.text.rome: A captain you know is sailing to Massalia and on to the coasts of Spain, taking passengers with goods. Those who come back will sell at three times the price. Those who don't won't care either way.
ev.a_voyage.text.athens: A captain you know is sailing to the Black Sea for grain and salted fish, taking passengers with goods. Those who come back will sell at three times the price. Those who don't won't care either way.
ev.a_voyage.text.egypt: A caravan is heading for the Red Sea ports, where ships leave for incense and spices. Those who come back will sell at three times the price. Those who don't won't care either way.
ev.a_voyage.go.success: The voyage paid off: the goods sold out the first day, and you came home sunburnt, with a full purse and a dozen stories.
ev.a_voyage.go.failure: A storm scattered the cargo, and you barely made it to shore. At least you're alive.
ev.a_voyage.send_goods.success: The captain came back honest and with a profit. A rare stroke of luck.
ev.a_voyage.send_goods.failure: The captain came back empty-handed with a long story about pirates.
ev.a_promotion.title: The Senior Post
ev.a_promotion.text: Your superior promises you the senior post if you name whoever has been stealing supplies from the storeroom. You know who: your workmate, who has a sick wife and three children.
ev.a_promotion.warn.success: He silently put everything back. The thefts stopped, and now he greets you like family.
ev.a_promotion.warn.failure: Your superior found out about the conversation. Now you are the one under suspicion.
ev.a_informer_past.title: A Shadow from the Past
ev.a_informer_past.text: The workmate you once informed on died long ago, and his son has grown up and now serves under your new superior. You are passed over for every task, and you know why.
ev.a_informer_past.apologize: Go to the son and ask forgiveness
ev.a_informer_past.apologize.success: He was silent for a long time, then said: "Father said you meant no harm." It became easier to breathe.
ev.a_informer_past.apologize.failure: He heard you out and turned away. Apologies, too, can come too late.
ev.a_hide_friend.title: A Knock at Night
ev.a_hide_friend.text: At night {npc} knocks at your door. The magistrate's men are in pursuit: the charge is theft from the treasury. {g=npc_sex:He|She} swears to be innocent and begs you to hide {g=npc_sex:him|her} until morning.
ev.a_hide_friend.hide.success: The guards looked in, poked a spear under the stairs and left. At dawn the fugitive was gone, leaving only a whisper: "I won't forget."
ev.a_hide_friend.hide.failure: The fugitive was found and led away, and you spent a long time buying your way out of a charge of harboring.
ev.a_hide_friend.give_money: Give money for the road, but don't let them in
ev.a_friend_repays.title: A Debt of Friendship
ev.a_friend_repays.text: {npc}, whom you once hid in your storeroom, was cleared long ago and has grown rich. Hearing of your troubles, {g=npc_sex:he|she} came in person — with a purse and the words: "This is a small part of what I owe you."
ev.a_peculium.title: The Price of Freedom
ev.a_peculium.text: An old servant of your household has been saving coppers for twenty years. Today he silently poured them onto the table — exactly what was once paid for him.
ev.a_peculium.text.rome: An old servant of your household has been saving his peculium for twenty years — the coppers his masters allowed him to manage. Today he silently poured them onto the table: exactly what was once paid for him.
ev.a_peculium.accept: Take the money and free him
ev.a_peculium.free_gift: Free him and give the money back
ev.a_peculium.refuse: Refuse: the household can't manage without him
ev.a_freedman_returns.title: The Freedman
ev.a_freedman_returns.text: Your former servant now keeps a shop by the city gate, and business is booming. As custom requires, he comes to pay his respects with a basket of the finest dates — and sends profitable buyers your way.
ev.a_boundary.title: The Wandering Stone
ev.a_boundary.text: Over the winter the boundary stone between your field and your neighbor's has "walked" about ten paces. For some reason it never walks in your direction.
ev.a_boundary.text.rome: Over the winter the boundary stone between your field and your neighbor's has "walked" about ten paces — and such stones are sacred to the god Terminus. For some reason it never walks in your direction.
ev.a_boundary.text.egypt: After the flood the field boundaries always wash away, and the surveyors measure out the plots again. But your neighbor got there first, and his field is suddenly a good ten paces wider.
ev.a_boundary.move_back: Move the stone back at night
ev.a_boundary.move_back.success: The stone is back in place. In the morning the neighbor scratched his head for a long time but said nothing.
ev.a_boundary.move_back.failure: The neighbor was lying in wait in the bushes. There was a fight, and by morning the whole village was talking.
ev.a_boundary.surveyor.success: The surveyor stretched his rope, counted the paces and gave you back your strip — plus a piece you didn't know you had.
ev.a_boundary.surveyor.failure: The surveyor measured for a long time, took his fee and declared that everything was "within the usual."
ev.a_boundary.talk: Invite the neighbor over for a jug of wine
ev.a_boundary.talk.success: By the third cup the stone was back in place — first in conversation, and by morning in the field. Since then you greet each other over the fence.
ev.a_boundary.talk.failure: The wine was drunk, and the stone stayed right where it was. A waste of good snacks, too.
ev.a_neighbor_helps.title: The Neighbor Over the Fence
ev.a_neighbor_helps.text: When a storm flattened your barley, the very neighbor you once made peace with over the boundary stone was the first to arrive with his sons and their sickles. Together you brought in the field before the next rain.
ev.a_house_fever.title: Fever in the House
ev.a_house_fever.text: The summer was stifling, and one after another the whole household fell ill. The fever shakes you every other day, as if on schedule.
ev.a_house_fever.text.rome: The summer was stifling, damp air drifts up from the low ground by the river, and one after another the whole household fell ill. The fever shakes you every other day, as if on schedule; no wonder the Romans built altars to the goddess Fever herself.
ev.a_house_fever.hills: Take the family to the hills
ev.a_house_fever.physician.success: The doctor prescribed infusions, daytime sleep and shutters closed against the damp air. A month later everyone was on their feet.
ev.a_house_fever.physician.failure: The infusions didn't help. The fever left when it pleased and took a good deal of your strength with it.
ev.a_house_fever.pray.success: The fever retreated. The neighbors credit the amulets; a doctor would credit the autumn. You're grateful to all of them.
ev.a_house_fever.pray.failure: The gods were silent. The illness wore you down to the bone.
ev.a_house_fever.endure: Ride it out like everyone else
ev.a_career_change.title: A New Road
ev.a_career_change.text: Twenty years of the same movements of your hands. A childhood friend invites you into his business: he carries goods along the coast and needs someone who can count and haggle.
ev.a_career_change.merchant: Buy in and take up trade
ev.a_career_change.learn: Stay, but learn to read in the evenings
ev.a_bakery.title: A Share in a Bakery
ev.a_bakery.text: The baker on your street is getting old and is looking for a partner: millstones, an oven, two donkeys and a queue around the corner every morning. He wants the money up front.
ev.a_bakery.invest.success: The bread took off: a queue at the door by dawn, empty shelves by noon. Your share is already paying for itself.
ev.a_bakery.invest.failure: The oven cracked in the very first winter, and half the money went into repairs.
ev.a_bakery.small: Invest a little, as a trial
ev.a_bakery.small.success: A little invested, a little earned. But no sleepless nights.
ev.a_bakery.small.failure: No profit came of it. Good thing you only risked a little.
ev.a_bakery_grown.title: Stamped Bread
ev.a_bakery_grown.text: The bakery you once bought into has grown: there are three ovens now, and the round loaves with your stamp are known throughout the district.
ev.a_marriage_strain.title: The Cold War
ev.a_marriage_strain.text: {npc} hasn't spoken to you for three days. A quarrel over a trifle has grown into reproaches for every year of your marriage, and no one remembers the trifle anymore.
ev.a_marriage_strain.text.rome: {npc} hasn't spoken to you for three days. A quarrel over a trifle has grown into reproaches for every year of your marriage. They say there is a shrine of the goddess Viriplaca on the Palatine, where married couples go to make up.
ev.a_marriage_strain.first_step.success: You began with a joke, and it ended in tears and laughter. Nobody ever remembered the trifle.
ev.a_marriage_strain.first_step.failure: The words came out wrong. The quarrel flared up again.
ev.a_marriage_strain.wait: Wait for it to cool down
ev.a_poor_debtor.title: A Debtor Without Money
ev.a_poor_debtor.text: The carter who has owed you for a whole year came empty-handed. You have every right to take his mules — but without the mules his family will be begging.
ev.a_poor_debtor.defer.success: Two years later the carter brought everything down to the last coin — and a little extra "for your patience."
ev.a_poor_debtor.defer.failure: The extra time passed and there's still no money. Now the carter crosses to the other side of the street.
ev.a_debtor_saves.title: A Meeting on the Road
ev.a_debtor_saves.text: On a deserted road robbers surrounded you — and then a cart came thundering around the bend: the carter whose debt you once forgave, with his three sons wielding clubs. The robbers scattered.
ev.a_collegium.title: The Brotherhood
ev.a_collegium.text: People of your trade are forming a brotherhood: a shared feast once a month, dues into a common chest, and when you die, a decent funeral at the common expense.
ev.a_collegium.run_for: Join and aim to lead it
